SMTO-LLM-0084 — An older Task couldn't use its Helper model

GUID: 2afd4f06-1ef0-592a-ac29-2b5d28197578
Slug: inference-helper-unavailable
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: helper_routing

What happened

  • A Task set up to use the Helper model couldn't use it, because the Helper's settings had changed or its model couldn't be confirmed. Current SMTO versions no longer show this for new work.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, expand Helper, and select Check saved model. This confirms the Helper's server is reachable and serves the model you chose.
  2. If the Helper's server or model changed on purpose, update its Endpoint and Model there, then select Save Helper. Saved changes apply to new work; the old Task keeps the settings it started with.
  3. Before starting again, read what the earlier Run already finished in its conversation, then send a new request for only what is left. This avoids repeating steps the earlier Run already completed.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model reports passing checks, and a new request runs without this message.

If it still fails

  • If brand-new work still shows this message, the server may be running an old SMTO version; select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't rerun the whole old Task from the start.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Historical identity: an accepted task's trusted Helper route could not be verified (its configuration changed, the model or chat template differed, or discovery could not confirm the served model); the retired HelperRouter no longer emits it.

What this means

  • The selector could not use its accepted helper route because the trusted configuration changed, its model/template requirement differs, or existing metadata discovery could not affirm the required served model. The existing selector failure path retains the capability ceiling; fallback requires an accepted primary-only preference.

Why this can happen

  • Helper configuration, template attestation or exact model membership could not be verified before generation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the request timeline and inference-pool ticket state.

How to fix it

  • This identity is only resolvable through catalog compatibility (resolve_error_ref in src/error_catalog/resolver.py). For an old run, check the saved Helper connection in Model routing and its diagnostics (POST /api/agent/model-routing/helper/diagnostics); if new work produces it, confirm the Server runs current code. Submit new work instead of altering the accepted task's settings snapshot.
  • Restore the accepted trusted helper configuration and the same served model/template, or submit a new task with shared routing or explicit primary fallback. Selection retains its existing capability ceiling and one-attempt policy.

Retry and execution caution

  • Restore the accepted trusted helper configuration and the same served model/template, or submit a new task with shared routing or explicit primary fallback. Selection retains its existing capability ceiling and one-attempt policy.

How to verify the fix

  • The owning pool has no unresolved transport and the selected endpoint meets accepted settings.

What not to do

  • Do not treat socket cancellation or URL separation as proof of backend completion or cache isolation.

Technical notes

  • No resource lease, operation receipt or capability grant is changed by admission diagnostics.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
